page: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The physical setup supplies 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs with symmetric multithreading, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, highlighted by top-quartile ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing at 61,947.22 points, PassMark CPU at 57,778.08, and Clang compilation scores reaching 42,205.0. Vector execution is reinforced by hardware-level AVX-512 and VNNI extensions, resulting in strong scores for cryptographic acceleration and small-model language inference. In contrast, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance levels across stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into middle percentiles, recording 166.18 GB/sec read and 67.32 GB/sec write speeds.

Cost efficiency is centered around dense memory and local NVMe storage colocation on a single dedicated-thread chassis. By bundling high-capacity ephemeral NVMe SSD space directly with 512 GB of RAM, the instance avoids the supplementary latency and detached block storage costs typically incurred with remote network volumes. However, the instance store is ephemeral, requiring external replication architectures for persistent state management.

The r6id.16xlarge is positioned for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, caching clusters, and data-intensive batch processing pipelines that require direct, high-throughput local disk caching alongside expansive system memory.
